Subject: SLA uplift packaging — BrightCart request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — BrightCart is keen to move forward but we have a tight internal mandate around availability and escalation. Our procurement and SRE leads asked if Redwood can provide a clearly staged SLA uplift package tied to commit levels. Specifically: 

- 99.95% baseline with standard support (included)
- 99.98% tier: 1.5x unit price, 4-hour P1 response (business hours)
- 99.99% tier: 2.5x unit price, 1-hour P1 response (24/7) + direct escalation to on-call lead

They also want explicit incident credit mechanics (per hour below SLO) and a 30% discount on the uplifted seat pricing if we sign a 24-month committed capacity minimum. Can you confirm whether Redwood can structure a concession for pilot pricing and what the earliest timeline for roll-out would be?

We'd like a compact proposal we can take to procurement next week. If helpful I can loop our legal contacts.

Appreciate it —
Alex
Sr. Infrastructure Program Manager
BrightCart

Attachments: none
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 12:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA uplift packaging — BrightCart request

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Internal note: looping Ben and Kimberly for pricing and legal carve-outs.

High level response we can offer for your procurement review (pilot -> GA path):

1) Pilot concession (3 months): one-time uplift waiver + 15% discount on uplifted unit price for the pilot period if commit >= 6 months post-pilot.
2) 99.98% tier: +1.5x unit price (matches your band) with 4-hour P1 response during business hours; escalation to dedicated TAM after 2 P1s in a 30-day window.
3) 99.99% tier: +2.25x unit price (we can move to 2.5x with contract term); 1-hour P1 response 24/7; guaranteed on-call lead escalation path with weekly post-incident sync for the first 90 days.
4) Credit mechanics: pro-rated hourly credit for downtime beyond the SLOs; we cap credits for repeated noncompliance and can add an SLA escrow in the enterprise amendment.

Concession note: to reach a 30% uplift discount we need a 24-month capacity commit with quarterly True-Up and a minimum monthly baseline (we propose 30% of committed capacity as baseline). Also recommend adding a canary fallback clause (auto-fallback to compatible model variant) to reduce incident surface for production cutover.

I attached a pricing sketch and a redlineable SLA exhibit (see attached). If that aligns, Kimberly/legal can prep language and Ben can confirm final TCV math.

Next step: Alex — would you prefer a short call with Ben/Kimberly or a tracked DocuSign with the exhibit for procurement?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Marissa / Kim — quick internal take:

- We can accept the pilot concession but limit the one-time uplift waiver to 60% of uplift margin for the pilot (protects revenue).
- For the 99.99% tier I'd prefer we start at +2.25x unit price and offer +2.5x as an earnout tied to an operational readiness review at month 3 (gives ops time to prove runbook efficacy).
- The requested 30% discount at 24 months: we can tier the discount (15% @ 12mo, 25% @ 18mo, 30% @ 24mo) with a 90-day true-up and an annual performance review.

Risks: the 1-hour P1 24/7 plus guaranteed on-call lead is expensive at low commit levels — we should make that a gated benefit that requires the 24-month commit or an add-on seat-based retainer. Also ensure our credit math caps at 20% of quarterly invoicing for repeat incidents.

Kimberly, please sketch the contract language for the canary fallback clause and escalation SLA. Marissa, if Alex wants DocuSign, ask procurement to send the contact and I'll quick-model the TCV with the tiered discount.

-Ben
VP, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

Alex — following internal alignment, here's a concise concession proposal you can present to procurement. If this looks acceptable we'll produce a redline-ready SLA exhibit and a short DocuSign envelope for signature.

Proposal (summary):
- Pilot (90 days): uplifted tier applied, with a 15% pilot discount on uplifted units. One-time uplift margin waiver capped at 60% of uplift margin.
- 99.98% tier: +1.5x unit price, 4-hour P1 response (business hours), TAM escalation after 2 P1s in 30 days.
- 99.99% tier (gated): +2.25x unit price at sign; conditional +2.5x after a month-3 ops review. 1-hour P1 response 24/7; on-call lead escalation as a gated benefit when contract term >= 18 months OR with purchase of a weekly retainer seat.
- Tiered long-term discount: 15% @ 12 months, 25% @ 18 months, 30% @ 24 months; quarterly true-up; minimum monthly baseline = 30% of committed capacity.
- Credits: pro-rated hourly credits beyond SLOs capped at 20% of quarterly invoicing for repeated incidents; first incident remediation support included (no credit).
- Operational terms: required canary fallback during production cutover, weekly post-incident sync for 90 days following a P1 for 99.99% customers.

Attachments: SLA_Uplift_Pricing_2028.xlsx (pricing sketch), BrightCart_MA_plan_v2.pdf (draft SLA exhibit).

If procurement wants a call to walk through, I'm available Monday 10–11am PT. Alternatively we can send a short DocuSign packet with the exhibit + order form. Which do you prefer?

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.
